title: California's 47th Congressional District election, 2026
description: California's 47th congressional district, covering portions of Orange County including Irvine, Laguna Beach, Laguna Niguel, Dana Point, and Tustin, holds a general election on November 3, 2026. Incumbent Democratic Rep. Dave Min, first elected in 2024, faces Republican challenger Jenny Rae Le Roux after both advanced from the June 2 top-two primary. The district has a Democratic voter registration advantage (36% Democratic, 32% Republican, 25% no party preference) and a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+6; Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Likely Democratic.' Min emphasizes his legislative record on gun violence prevention, environmental protection, and housing, while Le Roux campaigns on government efficiency and rooting out waste, fraud, and abuse through her role as executive director of CAL DOGE.
polling_note: No general election polls were found for this race as of mid-June 2026. The primary election was held June 2, 2026, and the general election is November 3, 2026.

candidates.name: Dave Min
candidates.summary: Dave Min is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 47th congressional district, first elected in 2024. He previously served in the California State Senate from 2020 to 2024 and was a law professor at UC Irvine specializing in banking and financial regulation. Min's campaign emphasizes his work on gun violence prevention, environmental protection, affordable housing, and domestic violence legislation, as well as his background prosecuting Wall Street fraud at the SEC.

candidates.name: Jenny Rae Le Roux
candidates.summary: Jenny Rae Le Roux is a Republican business owner and the executive director of CAL DOGE, a California government efficiency initiative. She holds a B.A. in Economics from the University of Virginia and an MBA from Columbia Business School, and previously worked at Bain & Company and as vice president of investments at Stillwater Equities before purchasing Management Consulted in 2012. Le Roux ran for governor in the 2021 California recall election and now campaigns for U.S. Congress on a platform of reducing government waste and fraud, cutting regulations, and making California more affordable.
